title: Quotient Functions and Denominator Exclusions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Given f(x) = sqrt(x + 1) and g(x) = sqrt(x - 1), determine the formula and natural domain for the quotient function (f / g)(x).

steps.title: Determine Individual Domains
steps.explanation: f(x) requires x + 1 >= 0, so x >= -1. g(x) requires x - 1 >= 0, so x >= 1.
steps.why: Even roots must have non-negative radicands to evaluate to real numbers.

steps.title: Identify Denominator Zeroes
steps.explanation: Division by zero is undefined, so any root of the denominator equation must be removed from the domain.
steps.why: Quotients f/g are undefined where the denominator function vanishes.

steps.title: Form the Intersection Domain
steps.explanation: Intersecting [-1, inf) and [1, inf) yields [1, inf). Removing x = 1 leaves the open interval (1, inf).
steps.why: Definition of quotient domain requires simultaneous validity and non-zero denominator.
